territorial_scope.description: Applies to controllers and processors established or ordinarily resident in Kenya, and to those not established in Kenya that process personal data of data subjects located in Kenya.

evidence.quote: not established or ordinarily resident in Kenya, but processing personal data of data subjects located in Kenya

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Kenya's Data Protection Act 2019 regulates processing of personal data by controllers and processors established in Kenya or processing data of persons located there. It creates the Data Protection Commissioner's Office and sets data subject rights, processing principles, registration, breach notification, transfer limits and penalties. Commenced 25 November 2019.
summary.long: The Act applies to processing of personal data by data controllers and processors that are established or ordinarily resident in Kenya and process in Kenya, and to those not established in Kenya that process personal data of data subjects located in Kenya (s. 4). It establishes the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (Part II) and requires registration of controllers and processors under thresholds the Commissioner prescribes (Part III). Part IV sets processing principles, data subject rights, consent conditions, rules on children's data, a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, impact assessments and breach notification (72 hours to the Commissioner, ss. 25-43). Sensitive and health data have further processing conditions (Part V). Transfers out of Kenya require proof of safeguards or listed grounds, and the Cabinet Secretary may require localisation for certain processing (Part VI). Exemptions cover personal, national security, journalism and research purposes (Part VII). The Commissioner handles complaints, issues enforcement and penalty notices, and may impose administrative fines up to five million shillings or, for undertakings, one per cent of turnover, whichever is lower (Part VIII). Offences carry fines and imprisonment, and a general penalty applies. Individuals may claim compensation from controllers or processors (s. 65).
